evidence.text: A rolling scalar can provide present acceleration without a positive stationary vacuum. The observationally allowed exponential supplies a small but nonzero field-space gradient whose scale is set by dark energy.

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: Select a stationary sector configuration, keep the remaining fields at specified values, evaluate the complete gradient norm, and divide by the complete potential. Apply the resulting local ratio to a conjecture that quantifies over field space.

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Fit observations directly in the physical model's parameter space with Bayesian MCMC, and independently profile the likelihood for the reported single-exponential check. This retains model information omitted by the envelope comparison.

sources.title: Dark Energy in the Swampland II

evidence.text: Transform the ellipsoid to a Euclidean ball, apply Cauchy-Schwarz, and inspect rotations at fixed eigenvalues. This agent abstraction isolates the geometrical mechanism behind possible sensitivity without claiming the paper used this exact formula.

sources.title: Reconstructing Quintessence

evidence.text: Plot sampled histories as trajectories, count bin visits and average local velocities. Group kinetic–potential paths with k-means, then inspect the representative endpoints for evidence of common evolution.

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: Estimate induced interactions by identifying nonvanishing diagrams, counting Yukawa and gauge vertices and loop factors, and enforcing the required soft or flavor-sensitive insertion. The method yields parametric sizes rather than evaluated amplitudes.

evidence.text: Minimize the gradient norm, verify the weights are accessible, and substitute into the full potential. The reconstruction separates geometric minimization from a dynamical-attractor claim.

sources.title: Swampland conjectures and slow-roll thawing quintessence

evidence.text: Determine whether a canonical scalar that begins nearly frozen can explain dark energy while meeting the paper's distance and refined de Sitter conditions. Assess how compatibility depends on initial slope, potential curvature, and observational priors.

sources.title: Multifield Cosmology and the Dark Universe

evidence.text: What cosmological effects arise from strongly non-geodesic multifield trajectories, and can reviewed exact inspiraling dark-energy solutions produce observable perturbation effects and potentially alleviate the Hubble and σ8 tensions?

sources.title: From Swampland to Phenomenology and Back

evidence.text: Can a scalar potential provide slowly evolving dark energy with density near 10^−120 MPl^4? The problem combines a tiny potential amplitude with sufficiently slow dynamics; satisfying one requirement does not establish the other.

sources.title: Swampland Conjectures and Late-Time Cosmology

evidence.text: Do cosmological distance and perturbation measurements permit canonical dark energy with an order-one potential slope or negative curvature, and do inferred field excursions challenge a Planck-scale distance limit?

evidence.text: How much can a canonical dark-energy scalar evolve while preserving the observed late-time expansion and linear perturbations?

sources.title: Finite-time Singularities in Swampland-related Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: The setting is late-time dark energy modeled by a canonical scalar with positive exponential potential on a flat homogeneous and isotropic universe. Its swampland connection is a reported constant-slope attractor identification; the paper does not enforce an explicit quantum-gravity inequality.

sources.title: Dark Energy, the Swampland and the Equivalence Principle

evidence.text: Can early suppression of a scalar-mediated dark-matter force permit appreciable attraction today while retaining acceptable expansion and structure formation? The paper also asks whether the interaction can slow quintessence sufficiently to accommodate a larger exponential-potential slope.

sources.title: Do We Live in the Swampland?

evidence.text: How can the present positive dark-energy density coexist with a conjecture excluding constant positive vacuum energy? The paper uses an extremely light rolling scalar with an exponential potential at the meV scale.

evidence.text: Can curved two-field dynamics generate stable late-time acceleration and observationally acceptable dark-energy transients even when the scalar potential is steep?

sources.title: Dark Energy and the Refined de Sitter Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a dark-energy scalar satisfy the negative-curvature branch while remaining observationally close to a cosmological constant? The example varies a hilltop height and tachyonic curvature, with its initial displacement controlling the amount of rolling.

sources.title: Multi-field dark energy: Cosmic acceleration on a steep potential

evidence.text: Can dark energy remain dynamically active on a steep potential while its equation of state resembles a cosmological constant? The paper investigates whether turning in field space permits this behavior and whether fluctuations can distinguish it observationally.

sources.title: Hubble sinks in the low-redshift swampland

evidence.text: Can dark-matter coupling produce apparent phantom dark energy while the scalar remains canonical? The adopted present normalization fixes a nonphantom effective value today, while evolution at positive redshift can change that behavior.
